summary: Aristotle C. Dy works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned PhDs from Ateneo de Manila University and SOAS University of London under Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013), and served as President of Xavier School and Lecturer at Ateneo de Manila.
Aritri Dutta is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She pursued an external PhD at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Henk Blezer (attested 2026).

Arjo Vanderjagt studied at Franklin Academy, Prattsburgh Central School, and the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arjuna S. R. specializes in computational studies, Indology, and philosophy. After studying at Karnataka Samskrit University (MA 2009–2011) and the University of Hyderabad (PhD 2012–2017), he held posts at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, including Assistant Professor and Assistant Registrar.

Arlo Griffiths works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard and Leiden (PhD 2004 under Henk Bodewitz), later holding posts at Cornell, Groningen, Leiden, the Kern Institute, and École française d'Extrême-Orient (Professor 2008).

Indologist Armand Guérinot studied under Paul Regnaud at the University of Lyon (PhD ~1893–1900) and Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn (~1898–1899). In 1909, he worked as an oriental typography proofreader at the Imprimerie Nationale.

Armand Minard studied at ENS, EPHE, and the University of Paris (PhD ~1928–1937) under Sylvain Lévi, Antoine Meillet, Theodor Bloch, and Louis Renou. He held posts at the University of Lyon (1933–1957), EPHE (1952–1976), and the Sorbonne (1957–1977).

Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval worked in linguistics and related fields. He was Professor of Vulgar Arabic at INALCO (1821–1871), Professor of Arabic at the Collège de France (1833–1871), and joined the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1849.
Armin W. Geertz is a scholar in religious studies. He held academic posts at Aarhus University, where he is attested in 2008 and became DVIP-emeritus and Professor Emeritus in 2019.

Arnab Bhattacharya works in computational studies and Indology. He studied at IIT Bombay (B.Tech. 1988–1992) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1993–1997), later serving at TIFR (2001), HBCSE (2021), and IIT Kanpur (Professor, attested 2024–2025).

Arnaldo Beltrami studied at the University of Turin (PhD ~1881–1885). Working in Indology and linguistics, he served as Docent of Greek at the University of Bologna and taught Latin and Greek at Liceo Ginnasio Luigi Galvani (1896–1931).
Arnav Anjaria studied at the University of Hyderabad (Integrated MA 2007–2014) and served as an Assistant Professor at Amity University (2018–2019), working in Tibetology and other fields.

Arnold Adriaan Bake studied at Leiden, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht (doctorate 1923–1930 under Willem Caland). A scholar of Indology and religious studies, he held posts at Leiden (1931), Brasenose College (1937–1944), and SOAS (lecturer 1948).
Arnold C. Taylor studied at the University of Oxford (~1886–1890, MA), working in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a schoolteacher at Uppingham School from ~1892 to 1925.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (PhD 1779–1784). He spent his career at Göttingen as Privatdozent, professor of philosophy (1794), and professor of history (1801).
Indologist Arnold Hirzel studied at the universities of Strasbourg and Munich, and completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig (~1888–1890) under the supervision of Ernst Windisch.

Historian Arnold J. Toynbee studied at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at King's College London (~1919–1924), Chatham House (~1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1955).

Arnold Kunst studied in Vienna and earned degrees under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak and Stanisław Schayer at the University of Warsaw (PhD ~1930–1934). He held posts at the University of Lviv (1929–1932), SOAS (1939, 1945–1947, 1963), and Cambridge.

Arsène Darmesteter studied at INALCO, École des chartes, and EPHE under Gaston Paris. A linguist, he held posts at EPHE (1872–1877), Séminaire Israélite de France, the University of Paris (1877–1882), and École Normale Supérieure (1878–1888).

Artemij Keidan earned his PhD at Sapienza University of Rome (2001–2005). Working in linguistics and Indology, he taught Russian at the University of L'Aquila (2009–2010) and became Associate Professor at Sapienza University of Rome in 2020.
